---
title: "Catchment Lake and Cancer InFocus"
---

Cancer InFocus (CIFTools, University of Kentucky Markey Cancer Center) is
the de facto standard tool NCI-designated centers already use to describe
their catchments — covering every designated center, with 35 licensed
adopters as of October 2024 and an active community around the CARDS group
and the Catchment Area Data Conference. Catchment Lake is not trying to
replace it.

## Upstream, not a competitor

Cancer InFocus gathers county-level data and produces standardized files and
a Shiny app for a center's catchment; that's a strength this project doesn't
try to duplicate. What Catchment Lake adds is what a snapshot-file tool
structurally can't do on its own: every release stays queryable, joins
across sources happen in SQL rather than by hand, and the whole thing is
reachable from R, Python, SQL, a browser, or an assistant — not only through
one application.

The intended relationship: Cancer InFocus (or ECCO, or any center's own
tool) reads *from* the lake, the same way a downstream consumer reads from
any published catalog. A recipe that writes CIFTools-shaped files for a
chosen catchment is a better path to adoption than a rival dashboard, and
the CARDS group is the audience this needs to reach before that recipe ships
([SPEC.md § Recipes](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-on-ice/blob/main/SPEC.md#recipes)
lists it as recipe 4, and open questions call out approaching the CIF team
directly before milestone M2 closes).

## What the lake cannot carry

Cancer InFocus's own county-level cancer *incidence* comes from the USCS
Incidence Analytic Dataset through special access — a bilateral or
Research-Data-Center arrangement between the requester and CDC/NCI, not a
public redistribution licence. A public lake structurally cannot republish
that: the [licence gate](licence-gate.qmd) rules out anything that isn't
redistributable by a third party, and special-access USCS incidence fails
that test regardless of how the data would otherwise be used. What Catchment
Lake carries instead is State Cancer Profiles' own *published* county
incidence and mortality rates — the same public route SCP itself uses, and
the one this lake keeps at every vintage rather than only the latest.

The ACR (American College of Radiology) Lung Cancer Screening Registry
facility locator is very likely proprietary and is not being pursued as a
source (SPEC.md's own licence-gate table).

No Cancer InFocus data values, coverage figures, or comparisons appear on
this site — anything about what CIF itself contains belongs to CIF and its
own documentation, not here.
